title: Ahi Poke
description: Cubed raw tuna dressed with soy, sesame and sweet onion, and given a short rest in the fridge so the seasoning takes. Nothing is cooked and nothing should be.
notes: Limu and inamona are what make this taste of the islands rather than of a soy dressing. Rehydrated wakame and crushed roasted macadamia are the usual mainland stand-ins and both are honest substitutions.

ingredients.name: limu
ingredients.note: chopped seaweed; rehydrated wakame stands in

ingredients.name: inamona
ingredients.note: roasted crushed kukui nut; macadamia is the common substitute

steps.text: Pat the tuna dry and cut it into even cubes with a sharp knife, drawing the blade through rather than pressing down.
steps.tip: A dull knife bruises the fish and you can see it — the cubes go cloudy exactly where they were crushed.

steps.text: Toss the tuna with the soy sauce, sesame oil and Hawaiian sea salt until every cube is glossy.
Fold through the sweet onion, scallions, sesame seeds, limu and inamona with a light hand.
Chill for a quarter of an hour to let the seasoning take, then serve straight from the fridge.
steps.tip: Do not leave it much longer than an hour. The soy starts curing the outside of the cubes and the texture turns firm and slightly chalky.
